findings.issue_text: [BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` meant to give flusher threads time after the drift change is a no-op, because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the intended wait never executes. The synchronization the comment promises does not exist: test_basic still relies on the flusher thread having produced before `step.join()` sets the stopped flag, so `(msg,) = messages` intermittently raises ValueError on unpack (empty list) whenever the thread has not flushed yet — the flake this line was added to fix remains, and the dead call masks it.

[BUG] `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is emitted with metric tag key "shards" while the same flusher's produce timer (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 192) use key "shard" for the identical `shard_tag` value. The wait_produce timer lands under a different dimension name than every other spans.buffer flusher metric: per-shard dashboards,_saved-views, and any alert scoped to tag `shard` silently miss wait_produce, and the flush pipeline's produce vs wait breakdown cannot be grouped in one query.

[BUG] The `--flusher-processes` click option (consumers/__init__.py) is an unbounded `type=int`, so a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` negative, builds `process_to_shards_map` from `range(<negative>)` (empty dict), and the round-robin `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError during SpanFlusher.__init__. An operator passing `--flusher-processes -1` gets a cryptic `KeyError: 0` crash loop at consumer startup instead of a validation error (one `click.IntRange` would fix it), and `--flusher-processes 0` silently means one-process-per-shard (the opposite of "no extra processes") because `0 or len(...)` falls back to the shard count.

[BUG] When a flusher runs as a thread (produce_to_pipe set) and is declared unhealthy, the new `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips kill and `_create_process_for_shards` immediately starts a second flusher for the same shards while the hung thread keeps running, since Python threads cannot be killed. A detected hang in thread mode now produces two concurrent flushers polling the same Redis segments — every segment is produced twice (duplicate spans in the output) — whereas the pre-change code failed fast with an uncaught AttributeError; the added `AttributeError` handler shows thread-mode restart was intended to be supported but it cannot be, because nothing ever stops the old thread.

[ADVISORY] `submit()` now calls `record_stored_segments()` once per per-group buffer, turning the consumer's per-message Redis work into `flusher_processes` round-trips where the pre-change code made one call on the full buffer (which `__init__` still receives and then discards). Operators raising `--flusher-processes` multiply Redis command load and submit latency linearly on the ingest path (e.g. 16 flusher processes -> 16 record_stored_segments pipelines per submit instead of 1); storing the original full buffer for parent-side bookkeeping deletes the `self.buffers` dict and this loop with identical behavior (the union of per-group shards equals the full buffer's shard set).

[ADVISORY] The Redis memory check likewise runs `get_memory_info()` once per per-group buffer on every gated submit, aggregating N calls whose shard coverage is identical to the single full-buffer call the code made before this diff. Each memory-gated submit issues `flusher_processes` Redis info round-trips instead of one (8 flusher processes -> 8x info commands per submit), and the used/available ratio only stays correct because duplicated per-node entries scale both sums equally — any later dedup or per-node change silently double-counts; reusing the retained full buffer deletes the loop.

[ADVISORY] The Python-level default `flusher_processes: int | None = None` resolves to one process per shard in SpanFlusher, while the CLI option for the same parameter added in consumers/__init__.py defaults to 1 — two contradictory defaults for one setting. Any construction path that omits the kwarg (a second consumer entrypoint, a script, out-of-tree code — and today every test in test_consumer.py) silently fans out to len(assigned_shards) child processes with that many Kafka producers and Redis clients where the pre-change code ran a single flusher; e.g. 64 assigned shards become 64 spawned processes, and test_basic already depends on the None->per-shard default, cementing the divergence.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is dead code — introduced by this diff but never called from anywhere; the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Six lines of unused method remain whose name promises per-shard restart but which actually re-create the entire process group (replacing it in `self.processes` without touching restart counters), inviting a future caller to misuse it; the deletion test passes — removing the method deletes lines with zero call sites to update.

[ADVISORY] The only new test for multiprocess flushing submits no messages and asserts only constructor bookkeeping (`len(processes) == 2`, mapping sizes), so no test in the diff exercises two processes actually flushing disjoint shard sets exactly once, the `_ensure_processes_alive` kill-and-recreate path, or the per-process backpressure rejection union. A regression in fan-out flushing (duplicated or dropped segments across processes) or in the restart path ships with production as the first place where more than one flusher process ever runs together; the new behavior-bearing code in flusher.py has no functional coverage in this diff.

[ADVISORY] In `join()`, once the deadline expires the `break` skips `terminate()` for every remaining process in the iteration, so child processes still alive at timeout are left running, whereas the pre-change code always called terminate after waiting. On a timed-out graceful shutdown, flusher children after the first are not terminated at join time and keep polling Redis and producing to Kafka until daemon teardown at process exit, racing with partition reassignment during consumer restart; only the first process is guaranteed a terminate.

[BUG] join() leaves the terminate() call outside the new per-process for loop (it sits at method-body indentation), so it force-terminates only the last-iterated flusher process and references the leaked loop variable 'process' after the loop. With multiple flusher processes, hung workers that ignore the stopped flag are never killed by join() and keep polling Redis and producing to Kafka after join() returns, until the daemon kill at parent exit; and when the consumer is assigned zero partitions, self.processes is empty, the loop body never runs, and the unbound name 'process' raises NameError inside join(), crashing the shutdown path that the old single-process code handled.

[BUG] flusher_processes/max_processes is never validated: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` turns 0 into one-process-per-shard, and a negative value makes num_processes = min(-1, len(shards)) = -1 so range(-1) builds zero flusher processes. An operator passing --flusher-processes -1 gets a consumer with zero flusher workers: spans are accepted into Redis and never flushed to Kafka, spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy never fires because there are no processes to monitor, and the invisible stall persists until Redis eviction; --flusher-processes 0 does the opposite of the operator's intent and spawns the maximum per-shard process count.

[BUG] The newly added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda returning None before it runs. The 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' synchronization does not exist: since flusher_processes now defaults to one thread per shard, the multi-threaded flush depends purely on the patched busy-loop picking up current_drift=9000 before step.join() sets stopped, so test_basic remains racy and fails with a ValueError on `(msg,) = messages` whenever the threads have not completed a flush cycle in time.

[ADVISORY] The completely rewritten health/restart logic in _ensure_processes_alive (dead-process detection, per-shard unhealthy metrics, the isinstance kill guard, restart via _create_process_for_shards, and the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) has no test coverage anywhere in this diff. Neither test in test_consumer.py nor the single tweaked assertion in test_flusher.py triggers a dead or hung flusher process, so a regression in the restart path — e.g. the isinstance guard skipping a kill or a restart that fails to recreate the worker — ships silently and surfaces as spans stuck in Redis while the consumer looks healthy, defeating the health monitoring this PR's title advertises.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code — the only restart path, _ensure_processes_alive, calls _create_process_for_shards directly — and its body starts a new poller for the shard's process without killing the existing one. Any future caller of this new method ends up with two live pollers on the same Redis shards double-flushing segments to Kafka; until such a call appears it is an untested, misleading API surface that should be deleted rather than shipped.

[ADVISORY] The new per-process metric tags are inconsistent and un-groupable: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes use tag key 'shard' while wait_produce uses 'shards', and all three encode the whole shard set as one comma-joined tag value instead of individual shard tags like flusher_unhealthy does. Operators slicing flusher timing by shard cannot correlate produce with wait_produce (different tag keys), and per-shard aggregation of the produce-path timers is impossible because a single tag value encodes the entire shard list, so the monitoring this PR adds cannot answer 'which shard is slow' for the metrics it tags this way.

[ADVISORY] On the thread-mode 'hang' restart path, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips killing the hung thread and _create_process_for_shards then immediately starts a second poller for the same shards while the original hung thread still exists. In produce_to_pipe/thread mode — the mode every test in this diff runs — a hang-triggered restart leaves two threads flushing the same Redis shards, so if the hung thread unblocks, segments are produced twice, yielding duplicate messages and flaky assertions in the tests exercising the multi-threaded flusher.

[ADVISORY] The API-level default contradicts the documented CLI default: max_processes=None resolves to one process per shard via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, while the click option defaults to 1 and the pre-diff behavior was always exactly one process. Any instantiation of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory or SpanFlusher that omits the new parameter (test_basic already does so implicitly) silently spawns len(shards) processes, each creating its own Kafka producer and connection set, instead of the single process the option's help text ('Defaults to 1') and all prior behavior promise; the default should be 1, not None.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only data-structure bookkeeping (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, process_to_shards_map contents) and never pushes spans through the shared processes before step.join(). The feature's core claim — that one process correctly flushes multiple assigned shards — is never verified end-to-end: if the round-robin mapping or the per-subset SpansBuffer(shards) construction reads the wrong Redis keys, every test in this diff still passes while spans from mis-mapped shards are silently never flushed in production.

[BUG] The new --flusher-processes knob is never validated: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy so `--flusher-processes 0` silently produces the maximum topology (one process per shard), and any negative value makes `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` negative, so `range(self.num_processes)` builds an empty process_to_shards_map and the round-robin loop raises KeyError when assigning the first shard. An operator who sets 0 (or a negative typo) via the CLI added in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py gets either maximum flusher fan-out -- the opposite of the configured limit, multiplying Kafka producers and Redis connections per consumer -- or an opaque KeyError crash at strategy creation instead of a configuration error, crash-looping the consumer.

[ADVISORY] The diff completely rewrites the flusher supervision logic (_ensure_processes_alive: per-process crash/hang detection, the isinstance kill guard, per-process restart counters, the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, per-shard unhealthy metrics) but no test in the diff exercises any restart, hang, or kill path. A regression in the restart path ships silently; when a flusher process hangs or crashes in production, the consumer either never restarts it (spans accumulate in Redis until backpressure rejects ingestion) or crash-loops -- the exact failure modes the PR title's 'Health Monitoring' claims to handle, and the renamed method (_ensure_process_alive -> _ensure_processes_alive) means no pre-existing test can be invoking it either.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no caller anywhere in the diff, and if it were ever wired up it would spawn a second live process for the same shards because it calls _create_process_for_shards without killing the existing self.processes[process_index] entry. The method is unexercised, untestable-by-construction work not traceable to any requirement, and the first future caller silently double-processes shards (two processes polling the same Redis segments) instead of restarting; deleting it removes 6 lines and the latent hazard.

[ADVISORY] join(timeout) spends the entire timeout budget on the first process in self.processes and, once the deadline passes, terminates every remaining process with no wait at all, so with flusher_processes > 1 the processes after the first get no drain window whenever the first one consumes the budget. During consumer shutdown or rebalance with the feature enabled, a hung first flusher causes all other flusher processes to be terminate()d mid-cycle with zero drain time, cutting off in-flight segment reads and Kafka produces for those shards -- a shutdown contract designed for one process that was structure-adapted but not semantics-adapted for N.

[ADVISORY] The same per-process shard list is emitted under metric tag key 'shard' for spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes (line 185, 195) but under tag key 'shards' for spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce (line 199). An operator building flusher health dashboards from this PR's metrics must query two different tag keys for one dimension; any query filtering wait_produce by shard=<list> -- the key its sibling metrics in the same loop use -- silently returns no series, so produce-vs-wait comparisons drop data.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten docstring states 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing,' but the same PR ships --flusher-processes with default=1 (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py line 434), so the operator-facing default creates a single process covering all shards, and the class default (None -> per shard) and the production default (1) are two divergent behaviors for one knob. An engineer reading SpanFlusher to plan capacity assumes per-shard parallelism is the shipped behavior and misplans flusher throughput and connection counts; tests that construct the factory directly exercise a per-shard topology that production does not run by default, so the tested configuration and the deployed configuration diverge.

[ADVISORY] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None, so the 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' wait never happens. The added lines do not fix the multiprocess timing race they were added for; the test still relies on the flusher threads' patched-to-no-op sleep causing a busy-spin to win the race against the '(msg,) = messages' unpack, and the comment tells future maintainers that timing is handled when it is not.

[ADVISORY] The CLAUDE.md hunk adds a generic Python union-narrowing style rule (hasattr vs isinstance on str | None) that is not traceable to the span-buffer multiprocess/health-monitoring intent of this PR. Unrelated drive-by documentation rides a feature PR, inflating its review surface and creating backport/merge-conflict exposure on a hot file, with no requirement in the PR pointing at it; it belongs in a separate docs-only change.

[BUG] SpanFlusher.join() skips terminate() for every flusher process after the first once the deadline expires, because the `break` on remaining_time<=0 exits the outer for-loop instead of advancing to the next process's terminate (and skips even process 0 when next_step.join(timeout) already consumed the budget). On any join called with a finite timeout (rebalance/shutdown), a flusher process hung inside an iteration — the exact case terminate exists for — is never killed for indices 1..N-1 and lives on as an orphan inside the still-running consumer process, continuing to poll Redis and produce segments for shards the rebalance handed to a new consumer's flusher, yielding duplicate span payloads in the downstream topic and orphans that accumulate across rebalances; the pre-diff single-process code always terminated after the deadline.

[BUG] The `time.sleep(0.1)` added to test_basic never sleeps because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' synchronization it claims to provide does not exist. The race the sleep was added to fix remains: step.join() sets the shared stopped flag immediately after the instant no-op, so a flusher thread that has not completed a poll since `current_drift.value = 9000` exits its loop without flushing, `(msg,) = messages` unpack fails, and the test flakes in CI while the comment claims determinism.

[BUG] In thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) the hang-restart path never stops the hung thread — process.kill() is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) and the AttributeError catch swallows nothing because kill is skipped entirely — and then _create_process_for_shards starts a second thread over the same shards. Two threads now flush the same shard set concurrently; when the hung thread resumes it emits segments through produce_to_pipe alongside its replacement, breaking the one-owner-per-shard invariant the health model assumes, where the pre-diff code failed loudly here (unhandled AttributeError on Thread.kill) instead of silently doubling the flushers.

[BUG] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` combined with the unvalidated click option makes `--flusher-processes 0` mean one process per shard (the maximum) and any negative value crash at startup, since min(-1, N)=-1 makes range(-1) empty while `i % -1` evaluates to 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError(0). An operator passing 0 intending to disable extra flushers gets the opposite — one spawned interpreter plus Kafka producer per shard — and a typo'd negative value kills the consumer at startup with a bare KeyError instead of a clear validation error, because the option in consumers/__init__.py uses bare type=int with no IntRange(min=1) bound.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer tags the shard dimension as `shards` while the produce timer and the segment_size timing a few lines above tag the identical value as `shard`. Dashboards and alerts grouping spans.buffer.flusher.* by the `shard` tag silently miss spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce entirely (its points land under a different tag key), and it can never be correlated with the per-shard flusher_unhealthy counter (single int shard) since the timers carry composite strings like "0,2" — the shard-level health view this diff advertises cannot be assembled.

[BUG] The added synchronization line `time.sleep(0.1)` is dead in this test because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op lambda at the top of the same test function, so the guard the diff adds to make test_basic deterministic exercises nothing. CI keeps flaking on the drift-advance vs step.join() race the line was added to close, and the next maintainer trusts a comment ('Give flusher threads time to process') describing behavior the code does not implement.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code — no caller exists anywhere in the diff — and its comment says it 'restarts' the process for a shard, but the implementation calls _create_process_for_shards, which spawns a new process for the same shard set without killing or joining the old one and overwrites self.processes[process_index], losing the handle to the still-running old process. The obvious next change (wiring per-shard restart, as the docstring advertises) silently double-spawns a flusher over the same shards and duplicates segment production; today the method is untested dead weight that misdocuments the restart path _ensure_processes_alive actually takes.

[ADVISORY] The new flusher_processes setting has two conflicting defaults: the CLI option documents "Defaults to 1" (consumers/__init__.py) while the factory/constructor default of None makes SpanFlusher compute max_processes = len(assigned_shards), i.e. one process per shard. Any construction path that omits the kwarg — as test_basic in this same diff already does — silently gets unbounded per-shard process fan-out (one spawned Python interpreter with its own Kafka producer per shard) instead of the documented single process, and the SpanFlusher docstring 'Creates one process per shard' now describes the non-default path, so the next embedder reading the help text deploys the wrong topology.

[ADVISORY] submit() now fires metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure") once per backpressured flusher process per call, where the pre-diff code incremented exactly once per call. Enabling --flusher-processes=P multiplies the counter's rate by up to P under identical Redis conditions, so rate-based alerts and before/after dashboard comparisons taken across the rollout report a backpressure increase that is purely an artifact of the process count.

[BUG] The hang-recovery path gates `process.kill()` on `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is false for the spawn-context processes this class creates (`multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`), so a hung flusher process is never killed before its replacement starts. On the exact failure the health monitoring exists to remediate, the hung process keeps running alongside the newly created one for the same shards — each further hang detection leaks another duplicate — so the same Redis segments are polled and produced to Kafka by multiple flushers (duplicate span segments double-counted downstream) while zombie processes and Kafka producers accumulate; the pre-diff code killed unconditionally before restarting, so the accepted restart contract was silently inverted.

[BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the same test begins by monkeypatching `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` (line 15), so the grace period the new comment promises ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') never executes. test_basic's outcome depends entirely on GIL scheduling racing the newly multiplied flusher threads against `step.join()`, so it intermittently fails under CI load with a ValueError from `(msg,) = messages` on an empty list, while readers of the comment believe the race was handled — the intended synchronization is simply absent.

[BUG] `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `--flusher-processes 0` as 'one process per shard' and passes any negative value through to `num_processes`, whose empty `process_to_shards_map` then raises `KeyError` on the first shard assignment. An operator or config system passing 0 silently gets maximum parallelism — one spawned process and Kafka producer per shard, the opposite of a zero limit — while any negative value crash-loops the consumer at startup with an opaque `KeyError` instead of a validation error.

[ADVISORY] The pre-existing alerting metric `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` silently changes meaning: one unhealthy process now emits one increment per shard in its group (with a new `shard` tag) instead of one increment per process. Dashboards and rate-based alerts on this existing metric see counts multiplied by shards-per-group (a 32-shard group reports 32x the old volume per detection cycle, repeated on every submit), so thresholds tuned before this deploy fire spuriously and historical comparisons break — the old observable contract was replaced without a rename or any documented acceptance.

[ADVISORY] The programmatic default (`flusher_processes=None` flowing into `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` in flusher.py line 52, i.e. one process per shard) contradicts the shipped CLI default of 1 (consumers/__init__.py line 434), and every test in this diff exercises only non-default configurations (test_basic via None, the limit test via 2). The shipped single-group production configuration — all shards in one process, including the all-shards metric tag and single-process restart path — has zero test coverage, so a regression there reaches production while CI validates only configurations production never runs; any future programmatic wiring of this factory also silently spawns one process per shard instead of the documented default of 1.

[ADVISORY] The new `shard` tag on the previously tagless metrics `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` carries a comma-joined per-process shard list rather than a shard id. In the default one-process deployment every datapoint is tagged with the full assigned-shard list (e.g. "0,1,...,31"), a value that changes on every partition rebalance, so the tag-value space grows without bound over time and per-shard aggregation is impossible — cardinality-limited metrics pipelines silently drop the series, defeating the health-monitoring objective the tags were added to serve.

[ADVISORY] `wait_produce` tags the shard dimension as `shards` while the sibling metrics in the same loop tag it as `shard`, and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with an int value rather than a joined list. Dashboards and queries grouping flusher metrics by `shard` silently omit flusher latency, and the same tag key carries two different value shapes (int vs comma-joined list) across metrics, so the monitoring surface this PR introduces is internally inconsistent before it is ever used.

[ADVISORY] `SpanFlusher` accepts the factory's `buffer` parameter but uses it only for `len(assigned_shards)`, constructing its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` per group so the injected instance is silently bypassed for polling, `record_stored_segments`, and memory checks. Any caller passing a configured or stubbed buffer — including tests — has that object ignored with no error, and the next parameter added to `SpansBuffer.__init__` (which the factory's construction site will pass) silently diverges from the flusher's bare `SpansBuffer(shards)` call, yielding differently-configured buffers in the two halves of the same consumer.

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` has no caller anywhere in the diff, and despite its comment it does not restart anything — it spawns an additional process for the shard's group without killing the existing one. The method is dead code today (deleting it breaks nothing), and the first future caller silently gets two live flushers polling the same shards with duplicate production, because the kill step that `_ensure_processes_alive` performs was never part of this path.

[ADVISORY] The max-memory-percentage guard now sums `get_memory_info()` across every per-group buffer without deduplicating Redis hosts that serve shards in more than one group. A host shared by k groups contributes k times to both `used` and `available`, so whenever host multiplicity is uneven across groups the `used/available` ratio departs from the single-buffer computation and the guard raises `MessageRejected` (pausing ingestion) at the wrong Redis memory level or fails to pause when it should.

[BUG] An unvalidated negative --flusher-processes value makes SpanFlusher.__init__ raise KeyError because range(num_processes) is empty while the shard-assignment loop still indexes process_to_shards_map, and an explicit 0 silently becomes one flusher process per shard via the `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback at line 52. An operator deploying ingest-spans with any negative flusher_processes value (typo, templating error) gets an unhandled KeyError('no_process'... actually KeyError: 0 from the empty map) on every consumer start, crash-looping the entire ingest-spans consumer; passing 0 contradicts the documented 'Defaults to 1' and silently escalates to one spawned process per shard (dozens of processes on high-partition topics) with no bound check at either the click option (consumers/__init__.py:432-437) or the factory.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer is emitted with metric tag key "shards" while the sibling produce timer (line 185) and segment_size_bytes timing (line 195) emitted in the same flush loop use tag key "shard", so the shard-scoped series lands under two different tag keys. Dashboards and alerts built on tags={shard: ...} for spans.buffer.flusher.produce never pick up the spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce series, silently dropping producer-wait latency from per-shard observability; any attempt to correlate produce vs wait_produce per shard joins on nothing.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is defined but never called anywhere in this change, duplicating the process-restart path that _ensure_processes_alive owns. The next maintainer who changes flusher restart bookkeeping (adding logging, reset logic, or metrics to restarts) updates _ensure_processes_alive and leaves this dead twin behind, or wires it in believing per-shard restart granularity already exists; deleting the six lines removes a divergent second implementation of restart semantics.

[ADVISORY] shard_tag is a comma-joined list of a process's assigned shards used as a Sentry tag and metric tag value, which mints a new tag value every time a consumer-group rebalance changes partition assignments, and is inconsistent with flusher_unhealthy (line 242), which tags individual integer shard ids. Metrics/telemetry per-tag cardinality fills with ephemeral values like '0,2' then '0,2,5' as rebalances recur, fragmenting per-shard dashboards and straining the metrics pipeline's cardinality budget; the same shard appears as '3' in flusher_unhealthy but as '1,3,7' in produce/wait_produce, so the two metric families cannot be correlated — a stable process_index or per-shard tagging serves both.

[BUG] The time.sleep(0.1) added under the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op lambda at its top (line 12), so the promised synchronization never happens. test_basic's only verification of the new multi-flusher produce path still depends on the flusher thread winning a scheduling race between fac._flusher.current_drift.value = 9000 and step.join(); on a loaded CI runner the thread is starved, (msg,) = messages unpacks an empty list and the test flakes — the diff's claimed fix for that flakiness literally does nothing.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten per-process health monitoring in _ensure_processes_alive — dead-process detection, hang detection, per-process restart counters, the post-MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, and kill+recreate — is triggered by no test in this diff; I checked tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py and tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py (the only test files changed) and neither kills a process, backdates process_healthy_since, nor asserts flusher_unhealthy or restart behavior, so only the healthy continue path ever runs via test_basic's submit(). The PR's headline health monitoring can be entirely broken (restart never fires, RuntimeError never raised, wrong shards reported unhealthy) and CI stays green; the diff updates exactly one assertion line in test_flusher.py, and any pre-existing restart test would have crashed on the removed self.process/healthy_since/process_restarts attributes, so none exists to catch a regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `--flusher-processes` click option (consumers/__init__.py) is an unbounded `type=int`, so a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` negative, builds `process_to_shards_map` from `range(<negative>)` (empty dict), and the round-robin `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError during SpanFlusher.__init__. An operator passing `--flusher-processes -1` gets a cryptic `KeyError: 0` crash loop at consumer startup instead of a validation error (one `click.IntRange` would fix it), and `--flusher-processes 0` silently means one-process-per-shard (the opposite of "no extra processes") because `0 or len(...)` falls back to the shard count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Click option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no bounds/validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and becomes `len(assigned_shards)` (i.e., potentially *more* processes, not “no extra”). If an operator passes `--flusher-processes -1`, `self.max_processes` becomes `-1` (truthy), then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes `-1`. That makes `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(-1)`), and the subsequent `process_index = i % self.num_processes` followed by `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will raise `KeyError` during initialization. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a flusher runs as a thread (produce_to_pipe set) and is declared unhealthy, the new `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips kill and `_create_process_for_shards` immediately starts a second flusher for the same shards while the hung thread keeps running, since Python threads cannot be killed. A detected hang in thread mode now produces two concurrent flushers polling the same Redis segments — every segment is produced twice (duplicate spans in the output) — whereas the pre-change code failed fast with an uncaught AttributeError; the added `AttributeError` handler shows thread-mode restart was intended to be supported but it cannot be, because nothing ever stops the old thread.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is running in thread mode (`produce_to_pipe` is not None, so `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread`), an unhealthy thread will hit the restart path. The code only calls `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, and it catches `AttributeError`, then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, which starts a new thread for the same shard set while the old (hung) thread remains alive (there is no thread stop/kill mechanism used; `self.stopped` is not set here). This can result in multiple concurrent flushers for the same shards. The finding’s comparison to the pre-change behavior is also supported: previously `self.process.kill()` would raise `AttributeError` for a `threading.Thread` and was not caught, effectively failing fast; now the added guard/exception handling enables a restart attempt that cannot actually terminate the old thread.

Operators raising `--flusher-processes` multiply Redis command load and submit latency linearly on the ingest path (e.g. 16 flusher processes -> 16 record_stored_segments pipelines per submit instead of 1); storing the original full buffer for parent-side bookkeeping deletes the `self.buffers` dict and this loop with identical behavior (the union of per-group shards equals the full buffer's shard set).

This makes per-message bookkeeping work scale with `self.num_processes` (derived from `max_processes` / `--flusher-processes`) rather than being a single call as before. The finding’s point that the original `buffer` passed to `SpanFlusher.__init__` is not retained (no `self.buffer = buffer` anymore) is also supported by the diff. This is a concrete perf/latency/Redis-load concern on the ingest path, not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes the Redis memory gating path from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating all per-process shard buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). Whether the returned entries are identical/duplicated per buffer can’t be proven from the diff alone (depends on `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` implementation), but the extra round-trips from the loop are directly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The hang-recovery path gates `process.kill()` on `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is false for the spawn-context processes this class creates (`multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`), so a hung flusher process is never killed before its replacement starts. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `shard` tag on the previously tagless metrics `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` carries a comma-joined per-process shard list rather than a shard id. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `wait_produce` tags the shard dimension as `shards` while the sibling metrics in the same loop tag it as `shard`, and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with an int value rather than a joined list. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `SpanFlusher` accepts the factory's `buffer` parameter but uses it only for `len(assigned_shards)`, constructing its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` per group so the injected instance is silently bypassed for polling, `record_stored_segments`, and memory checks. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` has no caller anywhere in the diff, and despite its comment it does not restart anything — it spawns an additional process for the shard's group without killing the existing one. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The max-memory-percentage guard now sums `get_memory_info()` across every per-group buffer without deduplicating Redis hosts that serve shards in more than one group. A host shared by k groups contributes k times to both `used` and `available`, so whenever host multiplicity is uneven across groups the `used/available` ratio departs from the single-buffer computation and the guard raises `MessageRejected` (pausing ingestion) at the wrong Redis memory level or fails to pause when it should.

The diff does not show `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()`, but given the new `ServiceMemory` import and the prior single-buffer behavior, it is plausible that multiple buffers can report overlapping Redis/service entries (e.g., same host serving shards in different groups), which would double-count and change the guard’s effective threshold. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An unvalidated negative --flusher-processes value makes SpanFlusher.__init__ raise KeyError because range(num_processes) is empty while the shard-assignment loop still indexes process_to_shards_map, and an explicit 0 silently becomes one flusher process per shard via the `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback at line 52. An operator deploying ingest-spans with any negative flusher_processes value (typo, templating error) gets an unhandled KeyError('no_process'... actually KeyError: 0 from the empty map) on every consumer start, crash-looping the entire ingest-spans consumer; passing 0 contradicts the documented 'Defaults to 1' and silently escalates to one spawned process per shard (dozens of processes on high-partition topics) with no bound check at either the click option (consumers/__init__.py:432-437) or the factory.

The click option added in `consumers/__init__.py` has `type=int` with no bounds check, and the factory passes it through, so this crash-loop is reachable from CLI configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] join(timeout) breaks out of the per-process loop the moment the deadline has expired, skipping process.terminate() for the current and every remaining process, so termination only happens for processes visited while time remained. On consumer shutdown with multiple flusher processes and an expired timeout, hung spawn processes — the exact case the health monitoring exists for — are never terminated: they keep polling Redis and producing segments through the shutdown/rebalance window, duplicating work with the replacement consumer instance; no test in the diff calls join with a timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, the per-process loop does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before reaching `process.terminate()`. This means once the deadline is exceeded, it stops iterating and never calls `terminate()` on the current process (the one where `remaining_time` went <= 0) nor on any later processes in `self.processes`. The diff shows no other shutdown/termination path for those processes, so with multiple flusher processes and an expired timeout, some spawned processes can remain alive past shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] max_processes is never validated and the arithmetic degenerates silently: 0 is falsy so 'max_processes or len(assigned_shards)' turns it into one-process-per-shard, and a negative value survives the or (truthy), makes min(negative, shard_count) negative, and range(negative) yields empty maps, constructing zero flusher processes. An operator passing --flusher-processes 0 gets the opposite of the requested limit (one process per shard), and a negative value deploys a consumer whose flusher silently does nothing — the empty self.processes/self.buffers dicts make _ensure_processes_alive and every submit loop iterate over nothing, so no health signal fires and spans accumulate unflushed in Redis; no test in the diff covers degenerate values or the min() clamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the diff sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `max_processes=0` (falsy) is converted into `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e. effectively “one process per shard” rather than honoring a 0 limit. There is also no validation against negative values: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative, and then `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` is empty while the subsequent `for ... process_index = i % self.num_processes; self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will raise (e.g. KeyError / modulo issues) for non-empty shards. The diff adds `--flusher-processes` as a plain `int` without bounds, and the added test only covers a positive value (2), so these degenerate cases are unhandled by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The comment 'Verify shards are distributed across processes' is not what the assertion does — assert total_shards == 4 only sums shard counts, so any assignment of the 4 shards across the 2 processes (including all four on process 0 with process 1 idle) passes. The round-robin distribution (i % num_processes) — the load-balancing property the feature exists to provide — is unverified, and a regression that piles every shard onto one process while the second idles ships green.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the comment says it verifies shards are distributed across processes, but the assertion `total_shards == 4` only checks that all 4 shards appear somewhere in `process_to_shards_map`, not that they are balanced across the 2 processes. Given the production logic uses `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, a regression that assigns all shards to one process could still satisfy this test, so the finding correctly flags an unverified (but intended) property of the new shard-to-process mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The per-process metric tags added in this diff are inconsistent: the produce timer and segment-size timing use tags={'shard': shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer uses tags={'shards': shard_tag}. spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce lands under a different tag key than the sibling metrics added in the same block, so dashboards and alerts built on the shard tag never see wait_produce and the three metrics of the same flush loop cannot be correlated.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, two metrics in the same flush loop use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` (`metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", ...)` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ...)`), but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", ...)` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. This is a concrete inconsistency visible in the diff and will cause `wait_produce` to be emitted under a different tag key, breaking correlation/queries/dashboards expecting the `shard` tag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) is newly added with no caller anywhere — _create_processes and _ensure_processes_alive both call the plural _create_process_for_shards, and since the method did not exist before this diff no unchanged code can reference it — making it dead code that would spawn a replacement for a shard's whole process without killing the old one. The dead, untested helper is a latent duplicate-production trap: any future caller gets two flushers polling the same shards (the self.processes[process_index] overwrite orphans the first, which is never joined or terminated), producing duplicate segments to Kafka; it should be deleted or wired and tested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` but no code in the shown changes calls it: initialization uses `_create_processes()` → `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, and liveness management uses `_ensure_processes_alive()` → `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. So it is dead/uncovered code in this PR. Also, as implemented, `_create_process_for_shard` would spawn a replacement via `_create_process_for_shards` without killing/joining the prior process for that `process_index` (it overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`), which is a concrete latent hazard if it were ever wired up. However, because it is currently unused, this is not a verifiable behavioral defect introduced by the diff, but it is a specific, actionable review concern (delete it or wire it safely + test).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit exercises no flusher behavior: it never calls submit() or poll(), never asserts the collected messages or commits lists, and assert len(flusher.processes) == 2 counts dict entries without checking the workers are alive or functional. A flusher whose two shared-shard threads crash on startup or produce nothing still passes, so the limit feature's functional behavior — limited processes actually flushing the full shard set — is unverified by the diff's dedicated test for it.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the code only constructs the strategy (`fac.create_with_partitions(...)`) and then asserts structural properties (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, shard distribution via `process_to_shards_map`). It never calls `step.submit(...)` or `step.poll()` (unlike `test_basic`), and it does not assert anything about `messages` or `commits`. As written, the test can pass even if the spawned flusher workers immediately crash or never flush/produce/commit anything, so it doesn’t functionally verify that “limited processes actually flush the full shard set,” only that the mapping/count fields are set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new flusher-processes knob is a deploy-time CLI flag defaulting to 1 — which reproduces the old single-process behavior — while every sibling flusher tunable consumed in flusher.py (max-unhealthy-seconds, backpressure-seconds, max-memory-percentage) is a runtime Sentry options entry, and the factory's own default (None, one process per shard) contradicts the flag's 'Defaults to 1' help text. The multiprocess flusher ships inert in production until someone passes the flag, operators cannot enable, tune, or roll back the process count without redeploying the consumer service (nor disable a bad value at runtime), and any code path constructing ProcessSpansStrategyFactory outside the CLI gets one-process-per-shard instead of the documented default of 1.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a deploy-time Click flag `--flusher-processes` with `default=1` and help text “Defaults to 1” (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), but the factory API defaults `flusher_processes: int | None = None` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py) and `SpanFlusher` interprets `None` as “one process per shard” via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` (flusher.py). This creates a real inconsistency: CLI default preserves old single-process behavior, while non-CLI constructions that omit `flusher_processes` get multiprocess-per-shard behavior, and unlike the other flusher tunables in flusher.py (`options.get(...)`), this new knob is not runtime-configurable. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded design/operability concern, not a directly provable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the produce_to_pipe (threading) mode a detected hang cannot kill the old worker — the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips process.kill() for threads — yet _create_process_for_shards unconditionally starts a replacement, so two flushers run over the same shards and the old thread is orphaned by the self.processes[process_index] overwrite. In any deployment using pipe/thread mode, a single hang-triggered restart starts duplicate segment production (the same Redis segments flushed and produced twice), and the orphaned thread is no longer tracked by join/terminate so it keeps producing after shutdown; no test in the diff exercises a restart in thread mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly supports a thread-based mode when `produce_to_pipe is not None` (`_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on an unhealthy worker it only attempts to kill if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung `threading.Thread` is not stopped. The code then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` and overwrites `self.processes[process_index] = process`, leaving the old thread untracked. Since both old and new threads run `SpanFlusher.main(shard_buffer, shards, ...)` for the same `shards`, they can concurrently flush/produce from the same Redis-backed segments, and `join()` only waits/terminates the currently-tracked threads/processes, not the orphaned one. No added tests cover a restart path in thread mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _create_process_for_shards constructs every per-process buffer as SpansBuffer(shards) from a bare list[int] of shard ids, but SpansBuffer is unchanged in this diff and is constructed by the factory with the shard-to-Redis-cluster mapping in assigned_shards, so assigned_shards[shard] inside each sub-buffer resolves to an int (or raises IndexError) instead of a Redis cluster handle. Every flusher process crashes with AttributeError on its first Redis operation; _ensure_processes_alive then restart-loops each process to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and raises RuntimeError, so the spans consumer crash-loops on startup even at the default --flusher-processes 1, halting span ingestion while segments accumulate in Redis until backpressure starts rejecting all Kafka messages. No buffer.py change ships in this diff to make the list construction valid.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral change: SpanFlusher now creates per-process buffers via `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` where `shards` comes from iterating `buffer.assigned_shards`. However, the finding’s core claim—that `SpansBuffer` requires a shard→Redis-cluster mapping and that passing a `list[int]` will make `assigned_shards[shard]` resolve to an int / raise IndexError—cannot be verified from this diff because `sentry.spans.buffer.SpansBuffer` is not shown/modified here. The new tests also instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=...)` and assert process/shard distribution without any observed crash, which weakly suggests the constructor may accept shard IDs. The asserted AttributeError/crash-loop chain depends on unseen `SpansBuffer` internals and Redis operations, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] join(timeout) computes remaining_time per process but only uses it to break out of the whole loop, so once the deadline expires while waiting on the first process every remaining flusher process is skipped without terminate(), whereas the old code unconditionally terminated its process once the deadline passed. On consumer shutdown or Kafka rebalance with a finite join timeout and a hung flusher subprocess, processes 2..N survive join() and keep polling Redis and producing spans through their own untracked Kafka producers while the replacement consumer's flushers take over the same shards, leaking processes and racing segment consumption on every rolling deploy; the later processes also get a strictly zero grace window because the first process consumes the entire timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the new multi-process loop breaks out of the *entire* `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` when `remaining_time <= 0`, so any processes after the first one are skipped entirely and never reach the `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()` call. This is a behavior change vs the old single-process code, which always called `terminate()` on its process after the wait loop. If the timeout is consumed while waiting on an earlier process, later flusher processes can remain alive after `join()` returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no call site anywhere in this diff, and unlike _ensure_processes_alive it spawns a replacement process without killing the process currently running for those shards. The next engineer who wires this method up as the per-shard restart API (its name and comment invite exactly that) silently runs two live processes over the same shards, and the self.processes[process_index] overwrite inside _create_process_for_shards orphans the old process object so it keeps polling Redis until daemon reaping; delete the method or make it kill the existing process first.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` (flusher.py) but there is no call site for it anywhere in this diff, so it is currently dead code. Its implementation calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly without first killing/terminating the existing process for that `process_index`. Since `_create_process_for_shards` overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` after `process.start()`, wiring this up later as a restart API would indeed risk leaving the old process running (orphaned) while a new one polls the same shards. This is a concrete maintainability/footgun concern grounded in the added code, not a presently-triggered defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer is emitted with tags={"shards": shard_tag} while the sibling produce timer and segment_size_bytes timing added in the same loop use the tag key "shard", splitting one logical dimension across two tag keys. Dashboards and alerts that filter spans.buffer.flusher.* by shard silently drop the entire wait_produce series, leaving on-call blind to producer-wait latency precisely while the new multiprocess flusher is being rolled out and evaluated; the tag key must be unified before the metrics ship.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff adds `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but the sibling `wait_produce` timer is emitted as `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency that will split the metric dimension across two tag keys and can break existing dashboards/alerts that filter on `shard`, but it doesn’t change core program correctness (it’s an observability/operability issue rather than a functional defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The programmatic default max_processes=None resolves through `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` to one flusher process per shard, while the CLI option added in this diff defaults to 1 (a single process covering all shards, i.e. the old behavior), so the same knob has opposite defaults depending on construction path. Every existing direct construction of SpanFlusher or ProcessSpansStrategyFactory - including tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py, whose base call sites cannot pass flusher_processes because the parameter did not exist - silently changes from one flusher to one flusher per assigned shard, multiplying processes/threads and Redis connection pools per instance without any code change on the caller's side.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `SpanFlusher.__init__(..., max_processes: int | None = None)` derive `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so omitting the argument now defaults to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` creates one process/thread per shard. In contrast, the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is added with `default=1`, preserving a single flusher process for the CLI path. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` passes `max_processes=self.flusher_processes`, and `flusher_processes` itself defaults to `None`, so existing programmatic callers that don’t set it will silently get per-shard processes/threads. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral/default inconsistency and potential resource-scaling concern, though not a provable correctness failure from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SpanFlusher.join exits its per-process loop via `break` once the deadline is exhausted, so every flusher process after the current one is never sent `terminate()` (the computed `remaining_time` is used for nothing else). On any join(timeout) where the first process or next_step.join consumes the deadline — e.g. a flusher hung on a Redis call during rebalance-driven strategy teardown — the loop breaks and all remaining hung flusher processes are left running with open Redis connections, invisible to the parent's health monitoring, and if the hang later clears they resume flushing shards the consumer no longer owns; the previous single-process code always reached terminate().
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the loop breaks when the deadline is exceeded, which prevents calling terminate() on remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard has no call site anywhere in the diff, and if ever wired up it starts a second process for the shard's group without killing the existing one. A maintainer using this evidently-intended per-shard restart API gets two processes polling the same Redis shards, producing every flushed segment to Kafka twice, while the old process is silently dropped from self.processes so no health check ever kills it; as shipped it is dead private code that misleads readers into believing per-shard restart is supported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` but shows no call sites for it (it’s only defined). As written, it calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without stopping/killing the existing process for that `process_index`; `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new process/thread and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`, so the prior process would be orphaned and could continue polling/producing for the same shards. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/safety concern, but it is not an active defect in shipped behavior given the lack of any wiring in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] submit now iterates every per-process SpansBuffer on each message, issuing one record_stored_segments Redis pipeline per flusher process (and one get_memory_info per buffer when the memory check is enabled) instead of a single call, and the parent permanently retains one Redis client per sub-buffer where it previously held one buffer. Operators who raise --flusher-processes toward the shard count multiply the consumer parent's Redis connection count and per-message Redis round-trips by that count (e.g. 256 pipelines per message on a 256-shard topic), and the memory check fetches the same shared Redis's ServiceMemory once per sub-buffer — N duplicate entries whose used/available ratio is unchanged, so the extra calls are pure Redis load added exactly when scaling the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__` now creating per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` stored in `self.buffers`), and `submit()` now loops over **all** buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and, when enabled, `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`. This concretely scales those calls with `num_processes`/`--flusher-processes`, potentially adding duplicate Redis work compared to the previous single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` / `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` design. The claim about multiplying per-message Redis pipelines and holding one Redis client per sub-buffer is a performance/operational concern grounded in these new loops and buffer instantiations (though the exact Redis client behavior is in `SpansBuffer`, not shown here), so it’s not a correctness bug but a significant scalability issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Because every flusher process polls the same Redis, a Redis brownout freezes healthy_since in all processes at once, so a single hang detection in _ensure_processes_alive kills and re-spawns all N flusher processes within one submit call, each spawn being a full spawn-context interpreter start plus sentry import. Under the most common hang cause (shared Redis latency exceeding spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds), a host already starved by the brownout absorbs N simultaneous process spawns per detection cycle where the previous design absorbed one, amplifying the brownout and delaying flush recovery; the new per-process health granularity only isolates process-local faults, which this thin poll-and-produce loop rarely has.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher from a single background worker to multiple per-shard(-group) workers (SpanFlusher.__init__ builds process_to_shards_map and starts self.num_processes via spawn in _create_processes). Health monitoring is also per-process: _ensure_processes_alive() iterates all self.processes and, if each process’s process_healthy_since is stale (hang) or not alive, it kills and restarts that process immediately within the same submit() call. If the common failure mode is a shared dependency (all processes blocked on the same Redis), then all processes can simultaneously exceed max-unhealthy-seconds and be respawned in one pass, potentially amplifying load; this is a real, diff-grounded operational/scaling concern, not a verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The wait_produce timer tags its metric as tags={"shards": shard_tag} while the sibling produce timer and segment_size_bytes timing added in the same block use tags={"shard": shard_tag}. An engineer building per-shard-group flusher dashboards or alerts against the `shard` tag (as emitted by spans.buffer.flusher.produce, spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, and spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy) silently matches no series for spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce, so produce latency is visible during an incident while produce-wait latency is absent with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use the `shard` tag, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This won’t break flushing behavior, but it will fragment observability/queries that expect a consistent tag key across these related metrics, exactly as the finding describes.
